newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market closed mostly down on Wednesday, with demand for funds decreasing in the absence of new A share issues and listings, traders said.

The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 9.48 percent from 10 percent on Tuesday. Turnover fell to 5.53 million lots from 7.19 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The repo rates have been hit by lower demand for funds due to a pause in the issuing of new shares," one trader said.
Traders expect the rates to regain ground later this week with the listing on Friday of three funds on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with market sentiment weak and some institutions continuing to sell, traders said.
The most active seven-year bond that matures in Nov 2003 fell to 97.30 yuan from 98.29 yuan on Tuesday. Turnover of the contract rose to 450 million yuan from 300 million.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market increased to 1.21 million lots from 1.07 million.
"The first seven-year bond hit its lowest level, falling below 98 yuan today, continuing its bad performance since it listed last week," said a local trader.
"The bond is likely to fall further with no recovery of market sentiment in the short term," he added.
